claims.text: A machine-learning approach can predict phase free energies of high-entropy alloys.
A machine-learning approach can predict derived fusion and high-temperature thermodynamic observables of high-entropy alloys.
The proposed machine-learning approach would reduce the cost of obtaining fusion and high-temperature thermodynamic properties.
The proposed machine-learning approach would increase prediction accuracy relative to explicit ab initio molecular-dynamics workflows and TOR-TILD.
The method applies to both solid and fluid states of high-entropy alloys.
The target conditions include high temperatures and pressures relevant to fusion and aerospace applications.
Configurational entropy and lattice structure are the structural mediators relevant to the proposed predictions.
Machine-learning algorithms can learn relationships between input features and target properties and use them to make predictions.
The accuracy of the machine-learning model depends on the availability of sufficient training data.
Phase free energies, melting points, and thermal-expansion coefficients can serve as benchmark observables for the proposed method.
